questions.question: What is the difference between a raft and a canoe?
questions.expected_answer: A raft is a flat platform made of logs or poles tied together that floats. A canoe is a narrow boat; a dugout canoe is made by hollowing out a single tree trunk, like the mokoro of the Okavango Delta.

questions.question: How were reed boats made, and why do they float?
questions.expected_answer: People cut and dried reeds, tied them tightly into long bundles and tied the bundles together into the shape of a boat. Reeds float because their stems are full of air. The ancient Egyptians made reed boats from papyrus on the Nile.

questions.question: How did sails change water transport? Give two examples of early sailing ships or voyages.
questions.expected_answer: Sails catch the wind and push the boat along, so people could travel much further, across seas and oceans, to trade and explore. Dhows with triangular sails traded along the east coast of Africa for over a thousand years. Bartolomeu Dias sailed around the Cape in a caravel in 1488, and Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498.
